title: The fall of the Berlin Wall
subject: histoire
description: On the night of **9 to November 10, 1989**, Berliners dismantled with their bare hands the wall that had divided their city for **28 years old**. A televised misunderstanding hastens the end of the Cold War.

hero.hook: The most guarded wall in the world falls... after a sentence dropped by mistake on television.

blocks.text: On the night of **9 to November 10, 1989**, Berliners from East and West attacked the wall that had fractured their city for **28 years old**. This moment marks the symbolic collapse of the [[Iron Curtain]], the border that cut Europe in two.
It's not just a popular festival. It's the result of a socialist economy on its last legs, a new Soviet course... and a botched press conference that opened the borders too soon.

sections.title: A wall to stop a people

blocks.text: After 1945, Berlin was divided into zones. Between **1949** and **1961**, more than **3 million** residents of , the German Democratic Republic (East Germany), fled to the West via Berlin. Often young and qualified. To stop the bleeding, barbed wire was laid on the night of **12 to August 13, 1961**, then a wall of **155 km**. [[GDR]]

blocks.caption: The fall of the Berlin Wall, November 1989.

blocks.text: The East German regime officially calls the wall the “Anti-Fascist Protective Bulwark,” claiming to keep spies in…rather than its citizens out.
Watchtowers, mines, dogs: **138** people are killed trying to pass through. West Berlin becomes a landlocked capitalist showcase. The wall is the concrete face of the Cold War.

sections.title: The summer when everything breaks down

blocks.text: With **Mikhaïl Gorbachev**, the Soviet leader, the USSR refused to crush its satellites as in 1968 during . 's reforms, transparency and restructuring, destabilize the bloc. In May **1989**, Hungary opened its border with Austria: the first real breach in the Iron Curtain. [[The Prague Spring (August 1968)]] [[Glasnost and Perestroika]]

In Leipzig, Monday demonstrations chanted “Wir sind das Volk” (“We are the people”). , the head of the GDR, who had promised that the wall would last for another “50 or 100 years”, was replaced in October. Too late: the movement is already irresistible. [[Erich Honecker]]

On **November 9**, **spokespersonGünter Schabowski** reads live a note that he did not have time to study. When asked when the new travel rules apply, he blurted: “Immediately, without delay. » In reality, it was planned for the next day.

blocks.caption: Crowd in West Berlin, night of November 9, 1989.

blocks.text: In **1988**, Bruce Springsteen sang in East Berlin in front of **300,000** people. Many see this concert as a moment of awakening for the youth of the East.

Berliners are rushing towards checkpoints and border posts. The guards, without instructions, finally opened. Around 11:30 p.m., at Bornholmer Strasse, the barriers gave way. German unity is being played out in the streets.

sections.title: From Berlin to the end of a world

blocks.text: Under the leadership of **Helmut Kohl**, Chancellor of West Germany, Germany was reunified on **October 3, 1990**. The shock takes away Poland, Czechoslovakia (), Bulgaria, Romania. The USSR itself disappeared in December **1991**. [[Velvet Revolution]]

blocks.text: The fall of the wall (**November 9, 1989**), triggered by a communications error, ushers in German reunification and accelerates the collapse of the Soviet bloc.
